question: If an item marked at ₹4,820 is sold for ₹4,338, then what is the discount percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplifying the ratio of Marked Price (MP) to Selling Price (SP):

MP : SP = 4820 : 4338

MP : SP = 10 : 9

Discount amount in ratio parts = 10 − 9 = 1 unit

Discount % = (1 ÷ 10) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹4820

Selling Price (SP) = ₹4338

**Formula Used:**

Discount = MP − SP

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

 
 Marked Price (MP) = ₹4820 Selling Price (SP) = ₹4338 
 SP part (90%) 
 ₹482 Discount 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount = 4820 − 4338

⇒ Discount = ₹482

⇒ Discount % = (482 ÷ 4820) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 10) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an item. The formula is Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts d₁% and d₂% are offered, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula: (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂/100)%.

Relation Between CP and MP

A direct relationship exists between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) using profit and discount percentages: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).
